\section{Gaussian Space --- Smooth Variation}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.SmoothVariation
\subsection*{Gaussian Space --- Smooth Variation: Introduction}
Positive-angle rotation quotients recover directional derivatives. Gaussian directional moments and nonnegative integral bounds then control Euclidean gradient length by normalized rotation variation, allowing infinite bounds.

\subsection*{Gaussian Space --- Smooth Variation: Results}

\begin{lemma}[Derivative along a Gaussian rotation curve]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasDerivAt_gaussianRotation_comp}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ have Fréchet
derivative $L$ at $x\in\mathbb R^n$, and let $y\in\mathbb R^n$. Then $\theta\mapsto
f(\cos\theta\,x+\sin\theta\,y)$ has derivative $L(y)$ at $\theta=0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Limit of absolute rotation quotients]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianRotation_difference_quotient_tendsto}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hasDerivAt_gaussianRotation_comp}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be differentiable at $x\in\mathbb
R^n$ with derivative $L:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$, and let $y\in\mathbb R^n$. As $\theta$
tends to $0$ through positive values, $|f(\cos\theta\,x+\sin\theta\,y)-f(x)|/\theta$
tends to $|L(y)|$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Absolute moment of a Gaussian linear functional]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_abs_gaussianLinearMap}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_abs_gaussianProjection, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianPDF}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on
$\mathbb R^n$, and let $L:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be a continuous linear functional. If
$e_i$ are the standard coordinate vectors, then
\[\int |L(z)|\,d\gamma_n(z)=\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^n L(e_i)^2}\,2\varphi(0),\]
where $\varphi$ is the standard Gaussian density on $\mathbb R$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Directional derivative bound from rotation variation]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.lintegral_gaussianRotation_derivative_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianRotation_difference_quotient_tendsto, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n\ge 0$, let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ have derivative at every $x$ given by the
linear functional $L(x)$, and let $C\in[0,\infty]$. Suppose that for every $\theta>0$,
the product Gaussian integral of $|f(\cos\theta X+\sin\theta Y)-f(X)|/\theta$ is at most
$C$, where $X$ and $Y$ are independent standard Gaussian vectors in $\mathbb R^n$. Then
the product Gaussian integral of $|L(X)Y|$ is at most $C$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Integrability of Gaussian linear functionals]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_gaussianLinearMap}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{4}
For every natural number $n$ and every continuous real linear functional $L:\mathbb
R^n\to\mathbb R$, the function $L$ is integrable with respect to the product standard
Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Absolute moment of a Gaussian linear functional]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.lintegral_abs_gaussianLinearMap}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_gaussianLinearMap, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_abs_gaussianLinearMap, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianPDF}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n\ge 0$, let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$, and let
$L:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be linear and continuous. Then $\int
|L(z)|\,d\gamma_n(z)=2\varphi(0)\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^n L(e_i)^2}$, where $e_i$ are the
coordinate unit vectors and $\varphi$ is the standard Gaussian density; the equality is
understood as an equality of nonnegative extended integrals, with the finite right-hand
side embedded in $[0,\infty]$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Gaussian moment identity for a family of linear functionals]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.lintegral_gaussianLinearMap_family}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.lintegral_abs_gaussianLinearMap, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianPDF}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n\ge 0$ and let $L$ assign to each $x\in\mathbb R^n$ a continuous linear functional
$L(x):\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$, continuously in $x$. Then the nonnegative extended
Gaussian integral of $|L(z_1)(z_2)|$ over independent standard Gaussian vectors
$z_1,z_2\in\mathbb R^n$ equals $2\varphi(0)$ times the nonnegative extended Gaussian
integral of $\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^n (L(x)e_i)^2}$ over $x\in\mathbb R^n$, where $e_i$ are
the coordinate unit vectors and $\varphi$ is the standard Gaussian density.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Gaussian gradient bound from rotational variation]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.lintegral_gaussianGradient_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussian_surface_normalization, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.lintegral_gaussianLinearMap_family, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.lintegral_gaussianRotation_derivative_le, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianPDF}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n\ge 0$, let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be Fréchet differentiable everywhere with
derivative $L(x):\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ at $x$, and suppose that $x\mapsto L(x)$ is
continuous. Let $C\in[0,\infty]$. If for every real $\theta>0$ the Gaussian integral of
$\sqrt{\pi/2}\,|f(\cos\theta\,z_1+\sin\theta\,z_2)-f(z_1)|/\theta$ over independent
standard Gaussian vectors $z_1,z_2\in\mathbb R^n$ is at most $C$, then $\int
\sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^n (L(x)e_i)^2}\,d\gamma_n(x)\le C$, as a nonnegative extended integral.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Gaussian gradient bound from mean rotational variation]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.lintegral_gaussianGradient_le_of_integral_variation_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.lintegral_gaussianGradient_le, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n\ge 0$, let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be Fréchet differentiable everywhere with
derivative $L(x):\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ at $x$, and suppose that $x\mapsto L(x)$ is
continuous and $0\le f(x)\le 1$ for every $x$. Let $C\in[0,\infty]$. If for every real
$\theta>0$, $\sqrt{\pi/2}$ times the Gaussian mean of
$|f(\cos\theta\,z_1+\sin\theta\,z_2)-f(z_1)|$, divided by $\theta$, is at most $C$ (with
that real quantity embedded in $[0,\infty]$), then $\int \sqrt{\sum_{i=1}^n
(L(x)e_i)^2}\,d\gamma_n(x)\le C$, as a nonnegative extended integral.
\end{lemma}
